title: Module manifest
description: The single entry point one module publishes so another may consume it. manhattan-bridge-3d publishes 'bridge-manifest.json' against this schema; dumbo-district-3d publishes 'district-manifest.json' against it. A consuming viewer needs no other knowledge of the producer: no source tree access, no build scripts, no shared geometry. This document is the whole dependency surface.

authoritative_for.description: Plain-language statement of what this module owns. Any asset outside this list MUST be consumed from another module, never rebuilt. This is the anti-duplication clause in machine-readable form.

depends_on.description: Other modules this one consumes. Declared so a viewer can resolve a whole stack from one root manifest.

required.description: When false, the consuming viewer MUST degrade gracefully if the manifest is absent. Every cross-module dependency should start life as optional so neither project can break the other's build.

georeference.description: Inline georeference, or a URL to one.

placement.description: Where this module's local engineering frame sits inside the shared scene frame. A module whose geometry is authored in its own frame (the bridge, origin at main-span midpoint) supplies this to become placeable. A module authored directly in the shared frame (the district) omits it.

modes.description: Viewer modes this module can participate in. A module that only supplies context geometry declares ['walk','map']; the bridge declares ['inspect','walk','map','tour'].

proxy.description: How this module appears inside somebody else's scene when it is NOT the focus. The bridge's proxy is what a pedestrian on Washington Street sees: correct silhouette, correct position, a few thousand triangles, no rivets. Publishing a proxy is what makes 'do not duplicate geometry' affordable for the consumer.

max_level.description: Highest LOD level a foreign consumer may refine this module to while it is a proxy. Caps the cost a neighbouring module can accidentally impose on a walk-mode frame budget.

handoff.description: How a viewer transitions from seeing this module as scenery to inspecting it in the owner's own mode, and back. This is the mechanism that lets one application host both a walkable district and a CAD-grade bridge without either team writing the other's UI. See VIEWER-MODES.md section 4.

entry_points.description: Named places a tour or a UI affordance can hand off at. A tour script references these by id.

preserve_camera.description: When true the consuming viewer keeps world camera position across the transition so the user never loses their place. Requires both modules to share a frame, which the contract guarantees.

ui_url.description: Optional URL of a self-contained UI bundle the owner ships for its own mode. Absent means the consumer renders only the shared metadata panel.

attribution.description: Credit lines a consuming viewer MUST display when this module's geometry is on screen.

extensions.description: Module-private payloads, keyed by the module_id that owns the convention. A consumer MUST ignore extensions it does not recognise. Use this rather than inventing top-level fields, which are rejected by design.

not_implemented_yet.description: Honest statement of gaps. A consuming viewer MAY surface these so a reviewer is never misled about what is real.

mode_id.description: inspect = CAD-grade examination of a single structure. walk = first-person traversal of a district. map = 2D plan view. tour = scripted playback, a driver rather than a renderer.
